classification.difficultyReason: Compare each pair of marks by expressing their deviations from different means in standard deviation units.

inlines.text: The following table lists the marks of several students on different tests in English and mathematics. Compare the English and mathematics marks of each student.

answer.short: English is better relative to the test results: $1$ standard deviation below the mean, compared with $\frac43$ standard deviations below for mathematics.
answer.worked:
In standard deviation units relative to each mean:
$$\begin{align*}\text{English}&=\frac{15-17}{2}\\\text{English}&=-1\\\text{Mathematics}&=\frac{13-17}{3}\\\text{Mathematics}&=-\frac43\end{align*}$$
David's English mark is one standard deviation below its mean; his mathematics mark is further below its mean. His English mark is better relative to the test results.

answer.short: English is better relative to the test results: $2$ standard deviations above the mean, compared with $1.75$ for mathematics.
answer.worked:
In standard deviation units relative to each mean:
$$\begin{align*}\text{English}&=\frac{42-30}{6}\\\text{English}&=2\\\text{Mathematics}&=\frac{39-25}{8}\\\text{Mathematics}&=\frac74=1.75\end{align*}$$
Akira's English mark is two standard deviations above its mean; the mathematics mark is only $1.75$ standard deviations above its mean. The English mark is better relative to the test results.

answer.short: Mathematics is better relative to the test results: $0.5$ standard deviations below the mean, compared with $1$ for English.
answer.worked:
In standard deviation units relative to each mean:
$$\begin{align*}\text{English}&=\frac{70-75}{5}\\\text{English}&=-1\\\text{Mathematics}&=\frac{65-70}{10}\\\text{Mathematics}&=-\frac12\end{align*}$$
Katherine's mathematics mark is half a standard deviation below its mean; her English mark is one standard deviation below its mean. Her mathematics mark is better relative to the test results.

answer.short: English is better relative to the test results: $\frac53$ standard deviations above the mean, compared with $1$ for mathematics.
answer.worked:
In standard deviation units relative to each mean:
$$\begin{align*}\text{English}&=\frac{70-55}{9}\\\text{English}&=\frac53\\\text{Mathematics}&=\frac{69-62}{7}\\\text{Mathematics}&=1\end{align*}$$
Daniel's English mark is more than one standard deviation above its mean; his mathematics mark is one standard deviation above its mean. His English mark is better relative to the test results.
